openings.claim: Material tags identify what to pick but do not resolve pattern-specific quantities. Rare sample consultation may leave that decision unsupported; an exact quantity checklist pencilled on each envelope could develop the incumbent's existing guidance and permit checking during filling.
openings.delta: Retain tagged trays and samples. Pencil the assigned pattern and its specified quantities on each envelope; mark each quantity only after its contents enter the envelope. Move checking into assembly. Evaluate this as a bounded probe, not a demonstrated solution for all 60 kits.
openings.prediction: With the same pattern mixture and shared trays, envelope quantity checks should reduce shared-material omissions. Exterior pattern names should also make assignments apparent. Writing and checking time must be included; the 90-minute full-run result remains unknown.
openings.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative is interference at shared trays rather than quantity confusion. It predicts that local loose materials will reduce omissions and crossing reaches even without envelope checklists, while checklists with shared trays may add time without improving completeness.
openings.defeat: A matched-mixture counterexample in which local loose materials eliminate omissions while shared trays plus correctly used quantity checklists retain them would defeat the proposed central explanation. O4 suggests this possibility but its unknown mixture prevents that conclusion now.
openings.probe: Using exactly two volunteers, compare small equal batches with matched pattern counts: incumbent assembly, shared trays plus pencilled checks, and local loose materials without checks. Alternate batch order. Independently count contents and record total preparation, filling and checking time, omissions and crossing reaches. Verify every arrangement stays within the existing table; stop within 90 minutes. Use only existing supplies and preserve specified quantities and dimensions. This tests the mechanism; successful small batches would still require a timed 60-kit run meeting the correction limit.
assumptions: The exact specified pattern quantities are available from existing sample kits.
The proposed small batches can be arranged within the existing table; verify before assembly.
Small-batch results may not transfer to the full pattern mixture or later supply depletion.
